verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,

Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, April 18, 2024, at 10:00 a.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on April 18, 2024, at 10:03 a.m.
  •  Present: Vice Chair Yank, Commissioners Viar, Zadorian, Pogosian, Aleksandryan, Chairperson
  Vidor
  •  Absent: Commissioner Tufenkian
  •  The Agenda for the April 18, 2024, Regular Meeting was posted on April 15, 2024, on the Bulletin
  Board outside City Hall.

2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or the
  audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such request before motion is proposed.

  a. Minutes of the March 21, 2024 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded :  Commissioner Viar

  Ayes:  Vice Chair Yank, Commissioners Viar, Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Tufenkian
  Abstain:  Commissioners Aleksandryan, Pogosian

3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Loreto Lopez, Program Coordinator
  • Ms. Lopez gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts &
  Culture locations.
  • Commission Zadorian and Chair Vidor gave an update on upcoming events in Glendale.

4. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS - NONE

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes. Members of
  the Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the Speaker, but there will be no Debate or
  Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
  - No Speakers

6. DISCUSSION ITEM(s)
  a. Artsakh Avenue Re-Development Project: Public Art
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave a summary and update on the Artsakh Ave.Re-Development Project.
  • Beau Basse of LeBasse Projects provided an update on the Artsakh Ave. Re-Development Project.
  He stated that in terms of options regarding the Artsakh public art, from Mr. Basse’s perspective,
  without having any understanding when Artsakh re-development project moves forward or how long
  the construction timeline might be, he suggested to find new opportunities and redistribute the
  funds, due to both art installations being site specific, and a challenge to relocate.
  1
 •  Vice Chair Yank stated she is in agreement with Mr. Basse’s assessment. Trying to find a new
  location for the current artworks doesn’t make sense because they are site specific to the locations.
  Commissioner Yank also stated that inviting the artist to submit a new proposal might be the best
  way to go. Commissioner Yank asked if there is a list of sites. Mr. Basse stated there are a list of
  sites. He stated that so much of the budget was tied up to the 3 sites on Artsakh and having a
  larger budget would allow to look into other sites. Mr. Basse stated that they would revisit
  opportunities that they were not looking at the beginning. Vice Chair Yank stated that her final
  thought is thinking of what could happen on Artsakh in the meantime, thinking creatively can there
  be a budget that is dedicated to temporary works or designs that are only created to be there for 3
  to 5 years to still have art on Artsakh Ave. during the transitional period. She stated she would hate
  to abandon it and nothing happen on Artsakh Ave. but maybe there is another solution like mural
  projects, something that is not going to be a giant cost to install and then remove and less
  permanent. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones said it was a great suggestion but that she has not spoken to
  Public Works, she also stated that creative crosswalks could be considered as a temporary art but
  would need to look at budget. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that they can look at potential temporary
  art or mural projects. Mr. Basse also agreed that is a great suggestion. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated
  that in regard to redistributing funds, she didn’t want the public to think artwork is not going to be
  installed on Artsakh, she stated once the construction bid is approved, funds can be reserved in the
  budget for a future time and reconsider the large art pieces. Vice Chair Yank asked for clarification
  as to when is the next update from Public Works? Ms. Fukutomi-Jones she would follow up but
  assumed it would be a few months.
•  Commissioner Viar stated that one of the great losses is the interactive feature of both installations,
  the draw to that location, so if a temporary piece can be put up that would have the same draw it
  would keep that as an art location in the public mind and looking for newer installations later in the
  future. She stated she would support Vice Chair Yank’s idea on temporary pieces to keep it as a
  concept of an art center in the public’s mind. Commissioner Viar wondered once Cathy Hrenda’s
  “Ride with the Wind” art installation is moved to another location, is there another art piece
  scheduled to be put in that location. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that there is no piece scheduled.
•  Commissioner Zadorian stated she doesn’t want to see the Artsakh Ave. art pieces elsewhere, the
  were specific to the area and agrees with all the Commissioners. She stated that she would rather
  wait it out until the next update from Public Works to make a final decision. She is also interested in
  knowing costs of moving and storage even though it was not an option. What is inflation specific to?
  Mr. Basse gave an example and essentially said is labor costs and materials and said in terms in
  storage is scale of fees adds up quickly. Commissioner Zadorian also asked about the Creative
  Crosswalks on Artsakh Ave., is that still possible? Ms. Fukutomi-Jones said it was tied to
  construction bid but can talk to Public Works and see if that is an option and the potential costs that
  would come out of Urban Art Fund.
•  Commissioner Aleksandryan stated that it was devastating to hear that the beautiful art pieces can’t
  be put up and that alternatives have to be considered for Artsakh Ave.
•  Chairperson Vidor stated she loved the idea of temporary art and after she got inquiries, she stated
  she wrote down Art Happens on Artsakh sort of like Art Happens Anywhere 2.0. She also stated
  that something should be done to make Artsakh vital and attract people to it. She stated that her
  opinion is that the art piece “Bountiful” tree could be scaled down to fit in place of Cathy Hrenda’s
  “Ride like the Wind”, that sits in front of the Central Library, that is in the process of being donated
  to the City and being relocated possibly to a park. She stated that the tree is monumental and that
  area is extremely visible and even though it’s not on Artsakh Ave. it’s almost like a gateway location
  and asked if there was any way “Bountiful “could be reduced in size to fit on the pad, because that
  location was also a garden and the idea of putting a tree in a garden with a huge amount of foot
  traffic would be a cool place to install. She also stated that regarding the “Tamir Gohar” art
  installation that’s a tough one to relocate but doesn’t want to give that one up, she stated that she
  would keep that one there. She stated that were her suggestions, to find another location and
  2
   possibly rescale the tree and that she really liked the space in front of the library that screams for
  art. She stated they’ll be drawn to see it and see all the temporary art on Artsakh Ave. She also
  stated that she has nothing against Public Works and that she knows they’re going to work really
  hard to make the project happen because it’s been so long in the making and it would just be a
  disaster to not have it happen but it’s going to be hard to get a realistic timeline because they way
  timeline works is that theirs inevitable delays and the timeline gets pushed. Chair Vidor asked Mr.
  Basse what the tolerance was for pushing it and is there any way the Commission could get
  reconfigured estimates of costs in 2026. Mr. Basse stated that fabrication bids do not lock in for
  more than 30 days so there is no chance of seeing anu estimates for 2026 but he agrees that he
  wouldn’t want to lose the art pieces but hopefully the artists are still interested 2026, 2027 or 2028
  depending how long construction on Artsakh Ave. takes, and if they’re still interested in making the
  pieces and seeing what the costs are and what the City has the budget for. Chair Vidor also asked
  what Mr. Basse’s technical assessment was to be able to reduce the size of the tree, still
  monumental but it would fit in the space by public library location. Mr. Basse stated that the artists
  are willing to scale down. He stated the tree hasn’t been fully engineered so the artists would be
  open to that. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that the pad that Cathy’s Hrenda’s piece “Ride like the
  Wind” sat on in front of Central Library was always intended to be for temporary art, so that location
  can also potentially be used for temporary art. Chair Vidor stated that everyone agreed that
  temporary art on Artsakh Ave. is a good idea and that the Commission start working closely with
  Public Works and find out what’s feasible and are willing to do. Chair Vidor stated that maybe at the
  next meeting Public Works can address the issue of temporary art and here an assessment of the
  extra work it will be creating.

  b. 2023-2024 Work Plan Progress
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones provided an update on the 2023-2024 Work Plan and stated Staff is still
  diligently working on the mural ordinance with the City Attorney’s office and hoping to have a draft
  very soon; Commission asked questions and provided their input.

6. COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS
  •  Commissioner Viar stated this will be her final meeting and thanked Staff and fellow Commissioners
  for their exceptional work with the Arts and Culture Commission. Commission, Staff and Student
  Commissioners thanked Commissioner Viar for her work with the Arts and Culture Commission.
  •  Commissioner Pogosian stated since April is Armenian History month, last week she attended a
  few Glendale events in remembrance of the Armenian Genocide. She extended her heartfelt
  congratulations to Ardy Kassakhian on his re-election to Glendale City Council, to Vartan
  Gharpetian to his successful campaign and return to City Council and Elen Asatryan for stepping
  into the role of new Mayor. She also thanked out going Council member Paula Devine for her
  dedicated service and contribution.
  •  Chair Vidor stated she had two comments that relate to potential agenda items. She stated one is
  looking at the page on the Arts and Culture Commission website that talks about Sponsorship and
  criteria obtaining sponsorship. She stated that what interests her is the $3000 -$5000 limit, she
  stated that maybe it can be broaden especially on the lower end and the due diligence on
  monitoring the sponsorship a review and placement of public art. She stated she’d like to review
  and, in the future, have an edited version. Chair Vidor also stated that the second discussion item
  she wants to talk about is the placement of public art. She stated that when art is donated or
  something is being placed that the Commission should have a say on where public art is placed,
  whether voting or not is another question. Chair Vidor is also curious to find out about an art piece
  at City Hall lobby, who donated it and she feels the Commission should have input in those types of
  decisions.

7. ADJOURNMENT 10:48 a.m.
  Motion to adjourn meeting.

  3
   Moved:  Commissioner Viar
  Seconded :  Commissioner Zadorian

The next Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is May 16, 2024, at 10:00 a.m., in City Council
Chambers (2nd Floor), 613 E. Broadway.
